title: Transaction layer framework - which body of law attaches at which stage
source: AUTHORED for MycOS Legal Agent 2026-08-29, adapted from an AI-generated Instagram carousel ('Arizona Transaction to National Bank', 12 slides, account joshua.aaron369719, self-labelled 'AI content'). The STAGE STRUCTURE is taken from that series. The 'applies' and 'caution' fields are this system's own evaluation and are not in the original. Not authority - a checklist for locating authority.
how_to_use: Walk the stages in order for a financed transaction. The federal layer is uniform in every state and is in reference/legal_agent/. The state layer must be resolved to the jurisdiction actually operating - see jurisdictions.json. Stages 8-11 are conditional and most retail transactions never reach them.
evaluation: Stages 1-7 describe an ordinary financed retail transaction accurately.

Stages 8-12 are each written conditionally ('may', 'if'), which is correct. But numbering them 1..12 in one sequence invites reading them as a pipeline every transaction traverses. Most do not: Reg T, Reg U and the '33/'34 Acts are not triggered by an ordinary auto or consumer receivable.
Citations spot-checked and accurate: 12 CFR 1002 = Reg B, 1026 = Reg Z, 220 = Reg T, 221 = Reg U, 12 U.S.C. 25b = the Dodd-Frank preemption standard codifying Barnett Bank.
The series' state layer is Arizona throughout. Arizona citations do not transfer to any other state - the uniform section numbers do.

stages.name: Transaction created
stages.key_inquiry: What was created on day one, who were the parties, and what terms and rights arose?
state_layer: State retail installment sales act, if a dealer-financed sale

stages.name: Credit application and origination
stages.key_inquiry: Who originated the credit, who reviewed the application, and what terms were created?
federal_layer: ECOA / Regulation B - 15 U.S.C. 1691 et seq.; 12 CFR Part 1002
TILA / Regulation Z - 15 U.S.C. 1601 et seq.; 12 CFR Part 1026 (consumer credit only)
stages.applies: usually - Reg Z reaches consumer credit; Reg B reaches any applicant for credit

stages.name: Receivable created and classified
stages.key_inquiry: What payment right was created, how is it classified, and who initially held it?
state_layer: Uniform 9-102 - account / chattel paper / payment intangible / instrument
stages.caution: Classification drives everything downstream: perfection method, priority rule and transfer rules all differ by collateral type.

stages.name: Security interest attaches
stages.key_inquiry: What collateral was identified, and what made the interest attach?
state_layer: Uniform 9-203 - value given, debtor rights in collateral, authenticated security agreement
stages.caution: Attachment is not perfection, not assignment, and not enforcement. Keep the four separate.

stages.name: Assignment or sale of the receivable
stages.key_inquiry: Who transferred it, to whom, and what rights actually moved?
state_layer: Uniform 9-109(a)(3) (sales of accounts/chattel paper are within Art. 9)
stages.caution: Ownership, servicing, collection rights and collateral rights can move separately. Ask which of them actually moved.

stages.name: Dealer funded or settled
stages.key_inquiry: Who paid or credited the dealer, from what source, and what did the acquiring creditor receive in exchange?
stages.applies: always - and this is an ACCOUNTING event
stages.caution: Funding the dealer is a distinct event from the buyer's repayment obligation. Transaction ledgers and assignment records evidence it; labels do not. This is also the exact point where 'the bank created the money from your signature' arguments enter. The inquiry is legitimate; that conclusion does not follow from it.

stages.name: State lender or servicer law continues
stages.key_inquiry: Which state lending or banking rules still govern, and who is carrying the account now?
state_layer: State licensing, consumer lending, motor vehicle finance, servicing and fraud law
stages.applies: if the holder is a state-regulated lender, finance company or servicer
stages.caution: Preempted for a national bank or its operating subsidiary - see stage 12.

stages.name: State blue-sky law
stages.key_inquiry: Is anything here actually a security under state law?
stages.applies: ONLY if the receivable enters securities activity
stages.caution: A receivable being sold or assigned is not by itself securities activity.

stages.name: Regulation T
stages.key_inquiry: Is a broker-dealer extending credit to finance or carry securities?
stages.applies: ONLY to credit extended BY a broker-dealer on securities
stages.caution: Not triggered by an ordinary retail installment receivable being assigned to a bank. Reg T governs margin credit at a broker-dealer.

stages.name: Regulation U
stages.key_inquiry: Is a covered lender extending purpose credit secured by margin stock?
federal_layer: 12 CFR Part 221, esp. 221.125 (credit to finance a purchase)
stages.applies: ONLY if the credit is purpose credit AND secured directly or indirectly by margin stock
stages.caution: Both conditions must hold. An auto or consumer receivable secured by a vehicle is neither.

stages.name: Securitization and federal securities law
stages.key_inquiry: Was a pool assembled and were interests in it offered or sold?
federal_layer: 17 CFR Parts 200-239 - Reg S-X / Reg S-K
stages.applies: ONLY if a pool was securitized and interests were offered
stages.caution: Securitization operates on the POOL and the certificates issued against it. It does not convert the individual obligor's contract into a security, and it does not by itself extinguish the obligation or the holder's right to enforce it.

stages.name: National bank and OCC preemption
stages.key_inquiry: Is the holder a national bank, and does federal law displace the state rule?
federal_layer: National Bank Act - 12 U.S.C. 21 et seq.
12 CFR Part 7 - OCC activities and operations
12 CFR Part 34 - OCC real estate lending
Barnett Bank v. Nelson, 517 U.S. 25 (1996) - 'prevent or significantly interfere' standard
state_layer: Whatever state rule is asserted - preemption is decided rule by rule
stages.applies: if a national bank or its operating subsidiary holds or services the account
stages.caution: 25b narrowed preemption after Dodd-Frank: it is case-by-case against the Barnett standard, not categorical. Do not assume a national bank holder displaces all state law.
